notes:
Summary: Closed-lost to direct OpenAI/Anthropic API decision. Primary reason: product simplicity + brand trust; they prioritized speed to market and fewer integration variables.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-11-03: Initial inbound via website form (AE: Jordan Price). Qualified; ecommerce personalization use-case.
- 2025-11-12: Intro call — outlined hosted API + Dedicated options. Customer emphasized speed and buying simplicity.
- 2025-12-02: Technical demo (Raya Kim). Showed routing/fallback and KV caching. Fireflies: ff_2025-12-09_ironwood-demo-01.
- 2025-12-15: Security questionnaire sent; asked about SOC2, KMS, VPC. Drive: security FAQ link.
- 2026-01-14: Security deep-dive with infra/security team. Long checklist; team expressed concern about onboarding timeline for Private. Fireflies: ff_2026-01-14_security-review.
- 2026-01-22: Procurement signaled a hard freeze for Q1 to re-evaluate vendor consolidation.
- 2026-02-10: Informal signal via procurement: choosing direct OpenAI for MVP due to fewer legal/ops touchpoints and existing corporate preference for OpenAI/Anthropic.
- 2026-02-15: Final call; "We want the fastest route to market — we'll use OpenAI/Anthropic for now." AE closed as lost.

Customer requirements and what we proposed:
- Workloads: high-volume chat for support agents + doc search/rerank for product pages. Latency target: p95 < 250ms for short chat turns; throughput spikes during sale windows. Cost sensitivity: medium-high.
- Preferences: prefer managed API with minimal infra involvement. Pinned model versioning nice-to-have but not blocker.
- Security: required SOC2 alignment, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, retention policy options and residency notes. They asked about on-prem only to evaluate legal requirements but were open to VPC.

Why we lost (raw):
- "Simplicity wins here" — PM said they have 2-week window to ship MVP and OpenAI direct API reduces vendor coordination.
- Procurement has pre-approved vendor list that includes OpenAI; speed + brand = lower procurement friction.
- Internal champion (Head of Product) moved to a different priority; no one pushed the deeper enterprise procurement track.
- Budget freeze in Q1 forced a low-effort stopgap rather than a dedicated/private deployment.
- Security: they were worried about time-to-validate Redwood Private; preferred the known path with existing OpenAI SLAs.

Competitive notes:
- OpenAI/Anthropic positioning: marketed simplicity, broad SDK support, and existing contracts with buyer.
- No technical blocker to Redwood — demo impressed, performance looked good in POC. This was a GTM/operational decision.

Next steps (post-loss):
- AE: Jordan to send concise loss summary + pricing comparison emailed to execs (done 2026-02-20). Gmail thread id thread:17542-openai-competitive-note.
- Sales ops to flag account for 6-month nurture (trigger: procurement re-open or performance/regret with chosen vendor).
- Product marketing: compile quick one-pager comparing integration friction and enterprise features vs direct APIs (Raya to draft). Drive doc path included.
- Security team: offer a templated onboarding checklist for Private/Dedicated to shorten validation time (idea to reduce future security friction).

Stated customer quote: "We need the thing that we can ship in two weeks — brand familiarity makes that the safe pick."

Other internal notes (short):
- Potential re-entry if they experience rate limits or cost blowouts on OpenAI/Anthropic; monitor usage signals if mentioned in public posts or recruiting pages.
- Keep link to security FAQ and INF-3421 ticket for post-mortem learnings.
